newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: AIB unit, Ark Life, says new business up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: AIB unit, Ark Life, says new business up in 1996.

text.p: Ark Life, the life assurance and pensions subsidiary of Allied Irish Banks Plc, said on Monday that new regular premium sales rose by 84 percent in 1996 to 23.0 million punts.
The growth came from new regular life business, which rose by 118 percent to 19.4 million, while new regular pensions business was maintained at 3.6 million.
Single premium sales totalled 101.5 million Irish pounds, a 57 percent increase on 1995, Ark Life said in a statement.
"Although our life, savings and investment business grew significantly in 1996, our pensions business remained static," managing director Fred Dinmore said.

"Last year we focused on the savings market and in 1997 our focus will be on the pensions market. We have undertaken a major revamp of our range of pension products and they now provide the most competitive charging structure in the Irish market," he said.
